_metadata.description: Requirements derived from the P1 operational targets in PRD.md.

requirements.title: Browser executor
requirements.description: Executes queued actions through browser-automation-studio, binding each identity to its own persistent session profile so that cookies and browser state never leak between identities. Sequenced last among P1 because it is the only capability carrying terms-of-service exposure, and everything above it must work manually first.

validation.notes: A dispatched action binds the identity's own session profile; two identities never share one profile.
A browser-executed action produces a record with the same fields as the manual executor produces.
Dispatch failure degrades the action to manual with the failure recorded, rather than marking it complete.
The browser executor is disabled for a platform until an operator decision recording the terms-of-service acceptance for that platform exists in DECISIONS.md.

requirements.title: Portfolio separation
requirements.description: Enforces minimum posting separation across identities and a ceiling on how many identities may post within a window. This is a cross-identity constraint that the per-identity queue cannot express, and it is what stops a portfolio from looking coordinated.

validation.notes: Scheduling a post inside the separation window of another identity's post is shifted or refused per policy.
The per-hour identity ceiling is enforced across the whole portfolio, not per platform.

requirements.title: Asset uniqueness
requirements.description: Refuses to queue a post carrying an asset that another identity has already published. Platforms hash duplicate media, so reusing a rendered asset across identities is a detectable coordination signal. asset-studio owns render provenance and answers the lookup.

validation.notes: A post whose asset ref was already published by another identity is refused with a typed error naming the prior identity.
An asset-studio lookup failure resolves to refuse rather than allow, matching the fail-closed posture used for eligibility.

requirements.title: Disclosure enforcement
requirements.description: Requires the platform's declared AI-content disclosure on any post from a persona-actor identity. The requirement is per platform and comes from the platform descriptor; the marketing canon defining which personas require disclosure is read-only input, not something this scenario decides.

validation.notes: A post from a persona-actor identity without the platform's required disclosure marker is refused.
A brand identity on the same platform is not subject to the persona disclosure requirement.

requirements.title: Retry classification
requirements.description: Classifies execution failures as retryable or terminal using per-platform rules from the descriptor, and backs off accordingly. A terminal failure such as a rejected credential must not be retried into a rate-limit penalty.

validation.notes: A transient failure retries with increasing backoff up to the configured limit; a terminal failure does not retry.
Retries consume cadence budget so that a retry storm cannot breach the platform ceiling.

requirements.title: Observation capture
requirements.description: Appends run outcomes to a program's observation log — which identity ran it, the gate measurements, whether it graduated or quarantined. This is the mechanism by which the speculative defaults shipped at P0 become measured, and it is append-only so that a revision never erases the evidence that motivated it.

validation.notes: Completing or quarantining a program run appends one observation carrying its measurements.
Observations are append-only; no code path rewrites or deletes a recorded observation.
A program with observations reports how many runs support it alongside its provenance confidence.

requirements.title: Publish metrics handoff
requirements.description: Returns post performance to content-desk so its ledger can answer how published work actually performed. This is the missing input that makes the marketing learning loop functional; without it, hook and post-type decisions are made on taste alone.

validation.notes: Metrics for a published post are attributable to the originating draft through the release identifier.
A metrics push that content-desk cannot accept is retried without duplicating the observation.

requirements.title: First-comment atomicity
requirements.description: Platforms suppress posts carrying external links in the body, so the standard practice is publishing the link as the first comment. A post and its first comment are therefore one unit of work, not two independent actions. Treating them separately leaves the operator to remember the second half and reports success when only the post landed.

validation.notes: A post declaring a first comment schedules both parts as one unit; the comment is never scheduled independently of its post.
A post that succeeds while its first comment fails is recorded as partially complete, not succeeded, and surfaces for operator attention.
The pair consumes cadence budget as two actions, since the platform counts two.

requirements.title: Per-platform post preview
requirements.description: Renders how a post will actually appear on its target platform using that platform's declared limits — where the caption truncates, how media is cropped to the platform's aspect ratio, and where the AI-content disclosure lands. The disclosure case is the one that matters most: a persona post whose disclosure is cropped out of frame is a compliance failure that is invisible until after publication.

validation.notes: Preview reports the caption truncation point derived from the platform descriptor rather than a hard-coded limit.
A required disclosure marker that would fall outside the visible region is reported as a preview failure, not a warning.
The preview surface renders for each configured platform and states which descriptor values produced it.

requirements.title: Environment liveness
requirements.description: Periodically verifies that an identity's environment still presents the region it attested to, and flags divergence. D-006 keeps environment *provisioning* out of scope and that stands; checking liveness is a different thing. An expired or rotated proxy silently breaks the scenario's core invariant with no signal, and it is the failure most likely to destroy an identity that took weeks to warm. This converts the unverifiable attestation recorded in SECURITY.md into a monitored one.

validation.notes: An observed region differing from the attested region raises a flag and pauses the identity's queue.
A liveness check that cannot complete is recorded as unknown and does not clear a prior divergence.
The check never reads or transmits a credential; it inspects egress properties only.
